svg.aria-label: The smoke cycle: the journey lane captures a path from an explorer, admits it once it held at every width and on a used instance, and proposes it as a generated suite in a pull request that the owner reviews and merges; CI runs the suite per browser project on every pull request and uploads its results; the lane reads those results, decides whether a break is a flake, a UI change or a bug, and proposes a quarantine, a heal or a baseline, or files a regression, again as a pull request.
svg.title: /journey smoke — one smoke cycle
svg.desc: One smoke cycle of /journey smoke has three places. In the lane, run from the main session on an instance of its own, smoke plan ranks the catalog and marks the journeys that need a path; a ui-explorer charted with path: wanted returns a path; smoke admit runs it twice, on a fresh and then a used instance, and stages it; smoke run re-runs the suite's paths in a seeded order, and with --perf measures them on Chrome; smoke propose checks every file and the pull request body with scrub and opens one pull request on an argus branch. In your repo, you review that pull request: merging accepts it, closing rejects it and the same change is never proposed again. In CI, the generated workflow runs the suite on every pull request: a matrix of browser projects in the pinned Playwright container (chromium, firefox, webkit, further viewports, a11y and i18n), msedge on the plain runner without screenshots, a non-gating quarantine job, and a baseline job that only a dispatch starts; each uploads its results for seven days. Back in the lane, smoke ci triages the run: a flake on the base branch is quarantined, never hidden; a moved control is healed after the unchanged expectations hold twice; a lost control or a failed expectation becomes a regression candidate that is replayed two of two and filed only after scrub finds no secret; a screenshot or ARIA difference is the owner's call; a missing baseline starts the baseline run, whose files smoke baseline adopts into a pull request that the owner reviews in the image view. Nothing is applied at run time, and sapu never merges a proposal.
svg.text: One smoke cycle, from a path to a pull request
A generated Playwright suite that your CI runs with no LLM. The lane proposes every change; you merge or close it.
the orchestrator, from the main session · an instance of its own · argus-live.mjs
A path is a short, fixed list of actions that ends in an expectation proving the journey's goal. Admitted only after every run holds.
Your repo: one pull request per proposal
on an argus/ branch · labelled agent-filed · sapu never merges it
In CI: your workflow, on every pull request
argus-smoke.yml · read-only token · actions pinned to SHAs · a fork's pull request runs nothing
Every job uploads test-results/ for 7 days. The suite runs --shuffle, retries once, and writes no baseline.
Back in the lane: what a break is
smoke ci reads the run; a script, never the explorer's word, decides
flaky on a push to the base branch
quarantine PR · tracking issue · still runs
flaky only on a pull request's head
a target matches nothing or several
heal-mode explorer · expectations hold twice · heal PR
an expectation or an action fails twice
failed on every attempt in CI, holds on Chrome
needs-owner issue with the run's link
a screenshot or ARIA snapshot differs
smoke ci shows the diff · --ids re-baselines
only CI's baseline job, on the pinned container, writes a screenshot or an ARIA baseline
A baseline that conflicts with the base branch is dropped and regenerated, never merged. msedge takes no screenshot.
· No LLM runs when the suite runs; the generator writes path data as JSON literals only.
· A normal CI run never writes a baseline, and a heal is never applied while a test runs.
· Every change is a pull request that sapu never merges; text from issues, docs and CI is fenced data.
· The suite drives loopback only. Fences are hygiene: the gates and your merge are the boundary.
